Subject: Dedicated burst / autoscale — need clarification on limits and pricing

Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re close to an internal decision but procurement has pushed back on the burst add-on economics and some of the operational limits. A few clarifying items: 

- For our expected baseline (10 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved), what is the hard cap for burstable capacity? Can we do 2.5x or 3x the baseline during spikes?
- How are surge rates billed (flat multiplier vs per-second metering)? We need predictable ceilings for monthly forecasting.
- Is there a cooldown after a burst event (how long before another burst can be triggered)?
- Do you offer deeper discounts for 12–24 month reserved commits that include the burst add-on as part of the package?

Procurement attached their standard PO form. Can you send a clear table our legal/finance can review?

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Wu

Subject: Re: Dedicated — burst add-on tiers, surge rates & discount proposal

Alex — great questions, and appreciated the PO form. I pulled our burst add-on options into a short table for clarity (see attached PDF v3). Summary below: 

Baseline: 10 GPUs reserved (A100-80GB equiv) – billed as Reserved Capacity.
Burst add-on (three configurable tiers):
- Tier A (short spikes): up to 150% of baseline concurrency, max 72 hours/month, billed at 1.25x the monthly Reserved GPU rate while active.
- Tier B (sustained bursts): up to 250% of baseline, max 36 hours/month, billed at 1.5x the monthly Reserved GPU rate while active.
- Tier C (emergency surge): up to 300% of baseline, max 12 hours/month, billed at 2.0x the monthly Reserved GPU rate while active; requires 24h notice for planned surges or explicit approval for on-demand emergency surges.

Surge billing specifics: metered hourly by the extra vGPU-equivalents consumed while bursting. We provide a hard-cap cost estimate each month based on the configured max-hours for the chosen tier so you can budget a ceiling.

Cooldown / rate limiting: after a contiguous burst window ends we enforce a configurable cooldown window. Defaults: 30 minutes cooldown for Tier A, 2 hours for Tier B, 6 hours for Tier C. These are tunable during onboarding and can be part of the SOW.

Discounting: standard Reserved commit discounts apply to the baseline capacity. For burst add-ons we typically offer: 10% off burst pricing for a 12-month commit (baseline + burst), 18% off for a 24-month commit. For strategic deals we can extend deeper one-time credits instead of recurring discount.

Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Burst_AddOn_Tiers_v3.pdf (pricing table + examples), draft SOW outline.

Happy to jump on a quick call with procurement to walk through the ceiling calc.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated — burst add-on tiers, surge rates & discount proposal

Karthik,

Thanks. A few follow-ups from finance: 
- The Band B (250%) maximum looks acceptable, but we need a guaranteed throughput SLA during burst windows: 95th percentile token latency under 250ms for text-gen at sequence length 512. Is that standard?
- Can the cooldown be shortened if we accept a higher surge rate? Procurement would consider a shorter cooldown in exchange for higher surge multiplier for Tier B/C.
- AtlasAI requests a one-time onboarding credit to offset the first-month spike costs if we need to test sustained bursts in Q2.

Also: Alex asked whether you can quote blended pricing on the SOW that factors in a 12-month commit with a 20% discount across baseline + burst. Please confirm if this is doable.

Regards,
Procurement Team
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@atlasai.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated — burst add-on tiers, surge rates & discount proposal

Procurement — quick responses inline: 

- Throughput SLA during burst windows: we can include a burst SLA for Tier B of 95th percentile P99 token latency under 300ms (sequence length 512). Operationally we run dedicated routing and prewarming for burst windows to meet this; P95 under 250ms is aggressive but we can commit to P95 < 275ms with a 12-month commit and a performance remediation credit if missed.

- Cooldown vs surge multiplier: yes — we can shorten cooldowns in exchange for a higher surge multiplier. Example: Tier B short-cooldown option = 1 hour cooldown at 1.65x (vs default 2.0x), or 30-minute cooldown for 1.8x. We documented these variants in v3 of the PDF.

- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time $25k test credit against burst usage for Q2 load testing with a signed 12-month reserved commitment. 

- Blended 12-month pricing at 20%: I need legal approval for a 20% across-the-board (baseline + burst). Laura, can we approve 20% for a 12-month committed deal if we use the $25k credit and lock in Tier B (250%, 36 hrs/mo) as the default add-on?

Thanks — I can put a redlined SOW with the blended pricing and the cooldown variants for review.

—Karthik
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated — burst add-on tiers, surge rates & discount proposal

Karthik — reviewed. Approve the following commercial concessions for AtlasAI: 

- 20% recurring discount for 12-month committed baseline + burst (blended).
- Include $25,000 one-time onboarding credit applied to first invoice (burst usage only).
- Tier B default: up to 250% baseline, 36 hours/month, surge multiplier capped at 1.65x for the short-cooldown variant (1 hour).
- SLA: commit to P95 < 275ms for seq_len 512 during burst windows; include performance remediation credit equivalent to 5% of monthly bill for missed SLA events (to be defined in SOW).

I’ll prepare a short redline for the SOW and send to legal. Keep the DocuSign flow gated until legal confirms final indemnities.

—Laura
VP, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
